newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain shipyard fire traps workers, kills 19.
newsitem.headline: Spain shipyard fire traps workers, kills 19.

text.p: Nineteen people were killed and 12 were injured on Thursday when a fiery explosion swept through a ship under construction in a Valencia shipyard, trapping workers inside, police said.
Police said they believed a fuel leak in the ship's engine room triggered the explosion, setting off a blaze that engulfed the lower decks.
"We believe 13 died at the scene and the remainder died in hospital," a police spokesman said.

Some workers, their faces blackened by the acrid smoke, fled in panic, escaping injury. But others were trapped inside the engine room and other sections of the ship, which was being built in the Mediterranean port of Valencia.
"I came up after I saw something breaking off the boat and all I could see was a cloud of smoke and a lot of fire and so we all ran out of the ship," one uninjured worker told reporters.
Survivors, their faces streaming with tears, stood by helplessly as fire-fighters battled the blaze and searched for bodies.
Family members kept anxious vigil awaiting word on whether their loved ones were among the victims.
"My son, my son," one woman wailed. He was only 18 and started working at the shipyard only a month ago.
The Valencia government declared a period of mourning and promised a full investigation.
Although the fire was small, the rescue operation was complicated by the fact that the fire was in the lower half of the ship's hold.
Two firemen were injured trying to control the blaze. At least 10 workers were hurt, most suffering only slight injuries.
A spokesman for the shipbuilders said many of the victims died as a result of suffocation and smoke inhalation.
The ship, named "Proof Spirit" and designed to carry chemicals, was being built for a Norwegian company. It was 110 metres long and 16 metres wide.
A port official said 17 of those killed had already been identified and came from four shipbuilding companies: Union Naval Levante, Inelca, Alfalavar and Insertank.
